Report on Recent San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Activities, Events and Announcements
items.text: Report on Recent San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Activities, Events and Announcements Ron Flynn, Acting General Manager (GM) provided an update regarding the recent algae bloom and actions being taken to reduce nitrogen levels in the San Francisco Bay. He emphasized that the SFPUC is in full compliance with current regulations and is working with regulators. He indicated the SFPUC is taking proactive steps to help reduce nitrogen in the bay via long-term investments including the state-of-the-art treatment plant being built on Treasure Island, which will have full-stream nitrogen removal (completion scheduled for 2026); piloting changes to the current treatment process to decrease nitrogen levels during dry-weather seasons; and repurposing existing tanks and other assets at the main wastewater treatment plant so they can be upgraded to removing nitrogen. He stated that the SFPUC is continuing to work with regulators on long-term strategies and are willing to adapt to meet potential nitrogen removal requirements as research and regulations evolve. He noted this will require long-range planning, construction of major new infrastructure, and billions of dollars in regional investments

items.title: Award Job Order Contract No. JOC-98, Electrical Construction, for work to be performed in San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, and Alameda Counties, in the amount not-to-exceed $5,000,000
items.text: Award Job Order Contract No. JOC-98, Electrical Construction, for work to be performed in San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, and Alameda Counties, in the amount not-to-exceed $5,000,000, with a guaranteed minimum task order opportunity amount of $50,000, and with a duration of two years, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, U.S. Electric Technologies, Inc., to perform C-10 licensed electrical construction work on San Francisco Public Utilities Commission systems and operations around the Bay Area. Commissioner Stacy questioned item 5a and why an increase in contract funds was necessary. Steve Ritchie, Assistant General Manager (AGM) Water Enterprise indicated the contract capacity was used up and additional funds are required for more work. Acting GM Flynn responded to a question from President Ajami regarding the social impact partnership program discussed under item 5a, indicating the program has no impact on the request for the additional funds. President Ajami discussed the “Funding and Cost” section under item 5d which indicates the Commission has the ability to increase the maximum contract amount by 50% of the original contract value and questioned how the 50% was determined. Ivy Fine, Contracts Division Manager responded that the language is taken from the Administrative Code and is for Job Order Contracts. President Ajami asked that staff look at how many contracts have used this provision

items.title: Award sole-source Grant No. CS-1245(G) to the Miraloma Park Improvement Club for the redesign of their Native Plant Garden Project at 350 O’Shaughnessy Blvd
items.text: Award sole-source Grant No. CS-1245(G) to the Miraloma Park Improvement Club for the redesign of their Native Plant Garden Project at 350 O'Shaughnessy Blvd., through the District 7 Participatory Budget Program, using addback funding in a not-to-exceed amount of $25,000 in accordance with Administrative Code Section 21G.8. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code Section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action. AGM Ritchie introduced the item. He responded to a question from Commissioner Stacy regarding the funding indicating that funds are received via the Board of Supervisor’s add-back process. Emma Heiken, Legislative Aide to Supervisor Melgar stated the funds were allocated by Supervisor Melgar through the participatory budgeting process, which she described
